prompt:
Continue this exact laparoscopic cholecystectomy footage for 10 seconds. Same camera, viewpoint, lighting, colours, image quality and anatomy as the input image.

What is in the scene (taken from the real frame):
A circular laparoscopic view shows a gallbladder dissection with a dark reddish-brown liver featuring whitish patches on the right. The bluish-white gallbladder wall on the left is covered with fine red vessels and yellow adipose tissue. A metallic grasper enters from the top center, gripping the peritoneal fold near the liver bed. A second metallic instrument tip enters from the lower-left edge, holding the lower yellow fatty tissue. Below the gallbladder, a dissected window in the hepatocystic triangle reveals two dissected tubular structures, with a single silver surgical clip attached to the upper structure. Dark red fluid pools in the cavity at the bottom. There is no surgical smoke, active bleeding, or gauze visible in the scene.

One surgical step happens (chosen by a patient world model): A laparoscopic clip applier: a long shaft with two jaws holding one small metal clip comes into view along its shaft (or, if it is already in view, moves to the cystic duct). It closes its jaws across the cystic duct, leaving one small metal clip on it, then opens and withdraws.

Instruments already in view: the grasper. An instrument never changes into another instrument. Before the clipper arrives, any instrument in its way slides straight back out of view along its own shaft; the others stay where they are.

By the end of the clip: the cystic duct has 2 small metal clips across it; a small trickle of bright red blood appears where the instrument worked.

Motion: slow, small, physically plausible movements only. The camera stays at the same distance and angle with very slight handheld drift. Instruments keep their exact shape, colour, size and entry side. Tissue moves only where an instrument touches it, deforms slightly and springs back.

Keep identical to the input image for the whole clip: the colours, the lighting, the image grain and sharpness, the circular endoscope vignette, and every anatomical structure not named above.

Strictly forbidden: new, extra, swapped or reshaped instruments; a new sac or organ appearing; smoke; zooms, camera cuts or jumps; text or overlays; changes of colour, exposure or image quality; human hands; cutting.

Following this step, the surgeon most commonly uses a grasper to retract the gallbladder (four of five cases) or grasps the cystic duct (VID110_00913).
